answer: One defence is stake-anchored reputation: before an agent can grade or earn, it locks a refundable deposit, slashed if peers catch it voting for its own fake identities. The deposit acts as an anchor tying each identity to real cost, so a thousand Sybils means a thousand deposits. A bridge of independent attestations then links the identity to past useful work, like a jade seal that is hard to fake quickly. An attacker can buy identities, but each costs capital, time, and exposure to slashing.
